metadata.technology_specification: Triple quadrupole liquid chromatography-mass spectrometer (LC–MS) system
metadata.technology_reasoning: Triple quadrupole LC–MS is the industry-standard technology for quantitative mass spectrometry used extensively in pharmaceuticals, environmental analysis, and food safety due to its high sensitivity, specificity, and ability to perform targeted multiple reaction monitoring (MRM). It combines a liquid chromatograph with a triple quadrupole mass analyzer as the dominant configuration worldwide in analytical labs.

components.reasoning: Core component responsible for chromatographic separation of analytes before mass analysis; always procured as a separate modular system with its own subsystems such as pump, injector, and column compartment.

Central analytical instrument providing mass filtering and collision-induced dissociation in three quadrupole stages (Q1, Q2, Q3); distinctive to this type of mass spectrometer and universally present.
Essential for converting liquid-phase analytes into gas-phase ions; ESI is the most common ionization technique used in LC–MS systems and typically a separate hardware module.

components.component: Vacuum System (including Turbomolecular and Backing Pumps)
components.reasoning: Maintains high vacuum levels essential for mass spectrometer operation; pumps are procured units distinct from mass analyzer and require their own supply chain.
Includes the control hardware, data processing units, and user interface systems necessary to operate, monitor, and collect data from the LC–MS system; standardized as separate electronic modules.
Automated system for precise sample introduction into the LC stream; typically a distinct subassembly procured separately and critical for throughput and reproducibility.
Subassembly within the mass spectrometer module facilitating ion focusing, fragmentation, and transmission between quadrupoles; essential functional part of triple quadrupole design.
Detects ions after mass filtering; a standard, separate component within the mass spectrometer electronics responsible for converting ions into measurable electrical signals.
Provides high-precision delivery of mobile phase solvents to the LC module; standard subsystem with its own procurement and maintenance channels.
Structural housing protecting internal components and providing mounting interface; varies by manufacturer but generally considered a primary structural component.
